newsitem.title: UK: Europe funds shift strategy amid rate fears -poll.
newsitem.headline: Europe funds shift strategy amid rate fears -poll.

text.p: The fear of rising interest rates and a more robust economic upswing has resulted in a big change in investment style among continental European fund managers, a survey by Merrill Lynch said.

The Gallup poll conducted in April said half of the managers who chose financials as their favourite sector last month have switched to cyclicals. Among industries, they prefer stocks in general engineering and electrical and electronics and do not like banks and insurance.
It also said that bullishness about economic prospects in the region may explain increased expectations of a repo rate rise over the coming year and further bearishness about German bonds.
The survey said there were fewer sellers of U.S. equities among continental European managers in April than March, and fewer buyers of continental European equities.
But on balance managers remained optimistic about stocks on the continent and bearish about U.S. equities on a three month view.
They were sellers of UK equities and keener on Japanese equities, while there was less buying of Pacific Basin equities and managers continued to raise their cash allocation.
They were sellers of bonds within and outside Europe.
The survey was carried out between April 3 and 9, covering 63 institutions responsible for funds totalling $511 billion. -- Andrew Gill, London newsroom +171 542 5887
